turn_text: Gordon Byrd here with Beyond the News from the WFLA Radio Newsroom. We have the privilege of speaking with U.S. Representative Laurel Lee, who won her first election to Congress from our part of Florida or the 15th District last November. Representative Lee has introduced her first bill. We've got to tell you about that first. It's a resolution honoring the Strawberry Festival in Plant City, which is wrapping up this weekend. Representative Lee, welcome to Beyond the News.
Well, thank you so much, of course. It's a pleasure to be with you today.

Now, I have to ask, how hard was it to lobby for this? I mean, did you have to bring up the strawberry shortcake makers or the chocolate fountain from Plant City? How difficult was it to persuade your colleagues to go along with this idea?

Well, I am glad to say that this is an idea that enjoys a lot of support in our delegation. And in fact, I'm very proud of the fact that that support is bipartisan. One thing that you will find in people who are from our area is that we all know and love Florida Strawberry Festival. So this piece of legislation was about as popular, I think, as they can be.

And that's no surprise. And now, of course, you've been doing some other work as well, even though this resolution is your first bill. You've been hard at work. You've been chairing the subcommittee on elections in the US House of Representatives. And today, as we speak Friday, the 10th, you held a hearing on the 2022 midterms and kind of a post-mortem kind of a look back. Of course, it's no secret. You have a lot of experience with elections as the former secretary of state of Florida. And what member what message rather should voters take away from what you found at the hearing today?

So we focus our first subcommittee hearing today on success stories from around our country. It is important that Congress does its work to shine a light on the election policies that are working. and states that are getting elections right. So today at our hearing, we had two secretaries of state. One was Secretary Kyle Ardon from Louisiana. The second was Franklin Rose from Ohio. And then we brought one of Florida's supervisors of elections, Chris Anderson from Seminole County. And each of them provided some really important testimony about their perspective on the elections administration. And some of the things they were doing in their states that have been very successful for them. This is a way that when we talk about the things that are working, that those ideas are things that we can then build on and share with other states around the country to implement those best practices.

Now, one of the things you mentioned in your opening statements at this hearing is the importance of sharing information among states. And in the news this past week, three states, including Florida, have pulled out of Eric, which is a system that, and you are surely more familiar with it than I, of checking voter rolls and sharing voter information between states to, among other things, I'm sure, make sure nobody votes twice. And I'm not going to ask you to second-guess Florida's decision, but I will ask about the role that Congress can play in encouraging states to keep sharing that kind of information, and if there's a congressional response to the situation with Eric.

Sure. Well, one thing that's important to understand is that elections administration and elections laws really begin and belong predominantly with the individual states. That's what our Constitution directs us to do, and we certainly respect those principles of federalism and Congress. So, you know, we are going to let states make decisions about the types of policies that they think are appropriate. And in Congress, our role is that we can work together in partnership with each of the states to help identify which of those practices have been successful. So that's why we began where we did today. We really took a look across the country at places that had been successful. And it hoped to really walk through the laws, also the pieces of administration and logistics And I'll tell you, a third piece that's really important when it comes to successful elections and elections integrity is cybersecurity and infrastructure. So one of my objectives as chair of this committee is to take a look at the things that we all share, the concerns that we all share that are universal across the country. And those concerns include things like emergency preparation, being ready for severe weather events, cybersecurity being assured that our cyber and digital infrastructure is prepared to meet any threats that it might face. And then also the physical infrastructure and voting systems and equipment, ensuring that we have standards for that type of thing and that we're helping share out those best practices and resources with the states so that they have the tools they need to be successful.

turn_text: Well, Representative Laurel Lee, you've now been a member of the United States Congress for at least two months and what's it been like in Washington?

Well, we are so fortunate to have a talented and experienced Florida delegation up here representing our state. The other members have been so welcoming to me And really the most important thing that we do is come up here to represent the people who elected us. And that means the values and the priorities of our community. And in some cases, it's an opportunity for us to really shine a light on some of the things that make our community special. And that's why I was so pleased to support my first bill since taking office, which related to plant city strawberry festival, because that is such a unique and special thing about Florida's 15th congressional district. We are the winter strawberry capital of the world implant city producing 75% of the nation's midwinter crop. And that's one of the things that makes Florida's 15th district special. So for me, serving up here in Washington, D.C., I have the opportunity to work on some really important policy issues. cybersecurity, elections, the many things that we'll be coming through to the Judiciary Committee. But I also get the privilege of getting to tell the story of our 15th district and all of the things that make it special.
